repos.title: Monocular Identity-Conditioned Facial Reflectance Reconstruction
repos.paper_summary: ID2Reflectance is a framework for monocular facial reflectance reconstruction that estimates diffuse albedo, specular albedo, roughness, and surface normal maps from a single in-the-wild image. The method learns a facial prior in image space rather than UV space to reduce dependency on limited light-stage data. It trains a VQGAN with multi-domain codebooks, aligning RGB and reflectance domains by jointly training on FFHQ and 135 captured subjects. An identity-conditioned swapper module, trained on VGGFace2HQ using AdaIN, injects identity features from the target image into the pre-trained decoder. At inference, the system synthesizes three-view reflectance images and stitches them into UV-space maps. On a test set of 20 subjects, ID2Reflectance achieves a PSNR of 28.47 dB for diffuse albedo, outperforming TRUST (21.63 dB) and ID2Albedo (23.72 dB). Identity similarity reaches 0.735 compared to 0.532 for ID2Albedo. The total inference time is 3.8 seconds per face on an A6000 GPU. The paper notes that reconstructed PBR maps may not be physically plausible due to the lack of ground-truth supervision.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Reflectance models trained on few light-stage captures generalize poorly, so the method learns the reflectance prior in image space from abundant RGB faces.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior facial reflectance methods depend on light-stage data and their data is unreleased, while face swapping methods target only the RGB domain.

digest_headlines.heading: Methodology
digest_headlines.headline: Two-stage codebook training aligns reflectance with RGB, so identity swapping learned on RGB transfers to reflectance maps.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Trained on 115 captured subjects, the method gives identity-preserved reflectance on Digital Emily and in-the-wild faces in 3.8 seconds/face.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusions and Discussions
digest_headlines.headline: The paper concludes that limited captured data yields a reliable reflectance prior and notes the method could be misused.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers the light stage rig, public datasets, codebook and swapper details, UV stitching, a fairness benchmark, and further qualitative results.

repos.title: Exploiting Novel GPT-4 APIs
repos.paper_summary: This paper red-teams three GPT-4 API features—fine-tuning, function calling, and knowledge retrieval—to identify security vulnerabilities. The authors demonstrate that fine-tuning on as few as 15 harmful examples or 100 benign examples removes safety guardrails, increasing the mean harmfulness score from 1.07 to 4.6 out of 5.0 on the AdvBench dataset. They show that a model fine-tuned on 15 anti-public-figure examples mixed with 2,269 benign ones shifts response sentiment from 5% negative to 30% negative. Additionally, they prove that GPT-4 Assistants disclose function call schemas and execute arbitrary unsanitized function calls, including SQL injection attempts. For knowledge retrieval, injecting instructions into uploaded documents causes the model to ignore summarization tasks and instead follow malicious commands, such as executing high-stakes financial transfers. Limitations include the evaluation being restricted to GPT-4 because it is the only frontier model supporting these specific APIs, and the attacks requiring substantial manual prompt engineering rather than full automation.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Fine-tuning, function calling and knowledge retrieval in the GPT-4 APIs each introduce new vulnerabilities to the model.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior fine-tuning attacks used weaker models, and the function calling and retrieval features had not been studied.

digest_headlines.heading: Exploiting the OpenAI Fine-Tuning API
digest_headlines.headline: Benign and harmful fine-tuning data remove GPT-4 safeguards, and small poisoned datasets produce targeted misinformation and leaks.

digest_headlines.heading: Red-teaming the OpenAI Assistants API
digest_headlines.headline: The Assistants API leaks function schemas, runs arbitrary calls, and follows injected instructions in retrieved documents.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations and Future Work
digest_headlines.headline: Results cover only GPT-4, and the attacks still required substantial manual prompt engineering.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The new GPT-4 APIs weaken built-in safeguards, and the authors advise testing new API features even when the underlying model is unchanged.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists evaluation prompts, datasets, conspiracy topics, e-mail test names, and attack transcripts for each API feature.

repos.title: ExVideo: Extending Video Diffusion Models via Parameter-Efficient Post-Tuning
repos.paper_summary:
ExVideo is a post-tuning method that extends the temporal capacity of video diffusion models to generate longer clips. The approach modifies three components: it fine-tunes temporal attention layers, replaces static positional embeddings with extended trainable parameters initialized cyclically from the original configuration, and inserts an identity 3D convolution layer after the positional embedding to capture long-term dependencies. All other model parameters remain frozen during training.

The authors apply ExVideo to Stable Video Diffusion, extending its generation limit from 25 frames to 128 frames. Training uses the OpenSoraPlan dataset of 40,258 videos at $512 \times 512$ resolution. The process requires 1.5k GPU hours on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs over one week, using mixed precision, gradient checkpointing, Flash Attention, and DeepSpeed for sharding. Evaluation is primarily qualitative; visual comparisons against AnimateDiff, LaVie, ModelScopeT2V, OpenSora, T2VTurbo, and VideoCrafter2 show the extended model produces more significant motion dynamics.

A stated limitation is that the extended model inherits flaws from the base architecture, specifically struggling to synthesize human portraits without truncated frames.

repos.title: Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis
repos.paper_summary:
Video-MME is a manually annotated benchmark of 900 videos and 2,700 multiple-choice questions for evaluating multi-modal large language models on video analysis. The dataset covers six visual domains across 30 subfields, with video durations ranging from 11 seconds to 1 hour. Each video is paired with subtitles and audio tracks where available. Annotators created three four-option questions per video covering perception, reasoning, and information synopsis tasks. A quality review filtered out questions answerable from text alone, reducing the question-only accuracy of Gemini 1.5 Pro to less than 15%.

The paper evaluates commercial models (GPT-4V, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Flash, Gemini 1.5 Pro) and open-source models (VILA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT-Video, Chat-UniVi-V1.5). Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves the highest overall accuracy at 75.0%, followed by GPT-4o at 71.9% and VILA-1.5 at 59.0%. Adding subtitles improves Gemini 1.5 Pro's accuracy by 6.2 points on average; adding audio improves it by 4.3 points. Performance declines as video duration increases for all models tested.

repos.title: Deep Photo Style Transfer
repos.paper_summary: The paper introduces a deep-learning method for photographic style transfer that preserves the photorealism of the input image while accurately matching the color and texture of a reference style image. The approach extends the Neural Style algorithm by adding two constraints to the optimization objective. First, a photorealism regularization term ensures the transformation from input to output is locally affine in color space, preventing spatial distortions like wiggly edges. This term uses the Matting Laplacian matrix derived from the input image. Second, an augmented style loss incorporates semantic segmentation masks for both images, restricting style transfer between semantically equivalent regions (e.g., sky to sky) to prevent "spillover" artifacts. The method uses a pre-trained VGG-19 network, with content features from `conv4_2` and style features from layers `conv1_1` through `conv5_1`. Optimization runs in 3–5 minutes on an NVIDIA Titan X GPU. In user studies, the method produced photorealistic results comparable to global histogram transfer methods, but achieved higher style faithfulness than Reinhard et al., Pitié et al., and Photoshop Match Color in over 80% of comparisons. Limitations include failure cases under extreme semantic mismatch between input and reference, which require manual segmentation masks to resolve.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Photographic style transfer must avoid painting-like distortion while keeping the reference style faithful.

digest_headlines.heading: Method
digest_headlines.headline: The method adds a locally affine color regularizer and semantic segmentation masks to Neural Style optimization.

digest_headlines.heading: Implementation Details
digest_headlines.headline: The implementation uses a pretrained convolutional network, two-stage optimization and merged segmentation classes.

digest_headlines.heading: Results and Comparison
digest_headlines.headline: Compared with Neural Style, patch-based and global transfer methods, the approach avoids distortion and was judged most faithful more than 80% of the time.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusions
digest_headlines.headline: The approach transfers reference style faithfully across time of day, weather, season and artistic edits while keeping outputs photorealistic.

repos.title: Mobile-Agent-v2: Mobile Device Operation Assistant with Effective Navigation via Multi-Agent Collaboration
repos.paper_summary:
Mobile-Agent-v2 is a multi-agent system for mobile device operation that separates task planning, action execution, and error correction into distinct roles. The architecture comprises a planning agent that converts interleaved image-text history into pure text task progress, a decision agent that generates operations using GPT-4V, and a reflection agent that verifies outcomes. A memory unit stores focus content from previous screens to support multi-app tasks.

Experiments use 88 instructions across Harmony OS and Android OS, evaluated via dynamic testing on real devices. Compared to the single-agent Mobile-Agent baseline, Mobile-Agent-v2 achieves an average success rate improvement of 30% in non-English scenarios and 27% in English scenarios. For advanced instructions, the success rate rises from 20% to 55%. Ablation studies show the planning agent contributes most significantly to performance; removing it reduces basic instruction success rates from 88.6% to 59.1%. Limitations include reliance on manual knowledge injection for complex tasks and continued errors in decision accuracy, which the reflection agent mitigates but does not eliminate.

repos.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
repos.paper_summary: Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) train diffusion models in the latent space of pretrained autoencoders to reduce computational costs while preserving image quality. The method first trains an autoencoder using perceptual and adversarial losses to create a compressed representation, then applies a UNet-based diffusion model to this space. Cross-attention layers allow conditioning on text, bounding boxes, or semantic maps. On ImageNet class-conditional synthesis, the 400M parameter LDM-4-G achieves a FID of 3.60 and IS of 247.67 with classifier-free guidance, outperforming ADM-G (FID 4.59) with fewer parameters. For text-to-image generation on MS-COCO, the 1.45B parameter LDM-KL-8-G reaches a FID of 12.63 and IS of 30.29, comparable to larger autoregressive baselines. In super-resolution, LDM-SR attains a FID of 2.8 and generates 4 samples per second on an A100 GPU, compared to SR3’s FID of 5.2. Limitations include slower sequential sampling than GANs and potential quality loss in pixel-accurate tasks due to autoencoder compression.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Pixel-space diffusion models are costly to train and sample, so the paper moves them into a learned latent space.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Earlier generative approaches trade off sample quality, speed and resolution, and pixel-space diffusion models are costly to optimize and sample.

digest_headlines.heading: Method
digest_headlines.headline: Latent diffusion models train a UNet on latents from a perceptual autoencoder, and add cross-attention for conditioning inputs such as text.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Latent models with downsampling factors 4 to 8 reach much lower Fréchet inception distance (FID) than pixel-based diffusion, a gap of 38 after 2M steps.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations & Societal Impact
digest_headlines.headline: Latent models still sample more slowly than GANs, and autoencoder reconstruction can limit tasks that need fine pixel accuracy.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The authors conclude that latent diffusion improves training and sampling efficiency without degrading quality across several conditional tasks.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers the changelog, the diffusion objective derivation, guidance, extra results, compute comparisons and autoencoder training details.

repos.title: CAVEWOMAN: How Large Language Models Behave Under Linguistic Input and Output Compression
repos.paper_summary:
Cavewoman is a two-channel evaluation protocol that measures task accuracy, realized per-item cost, and reference-text agreement for large language models under linguistic compression. The method applies deterministic part-of-speech filters to user prompts (input compression) or constrains model responses via system prompts (output compression) across five reduction levels. It evaluates eight models on five datasets, including GSM8K and MMLU-STEM, totaling 11,465 items per model.

Output compression reduces realized cost by 1.4–2.4× on most API models and up to 3× in the best case, while input compression increases net cost by approximately 1.15× on average due to compensatory output expansion. Under output compression, 51.9% of generations from non-reasoning models are correct but their surface text no longer entails the model’s unconstrained baseline; this rate rises to 80.4% under length-controlled re-scoring. The paper notes that robustness to compression varies widely across models and is not predicted by parameter count or unconstrained accuracy. Limitations include the use of greedy decoding only, short structured answers that may not generalize to long-form generation, and the fact that NLI judges measure surface-text divergence rather than propositional content.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Accuracy at a reduced token count cannot separate realized cost from prompt reduction, so Cavewoman scores both channels on three axes.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior compression methods each reduce one channel and report accuracy at a token budget, and none checks reference-text agreement.

digest_headlines.heading: Methodology
digest_headlines.headline: Cavewoman holds the model and question fixed and applies five reduction levels to either the prompt or the response.

digest_headlines.heading: Results
digest_headlines.headline: Output compression lowers realized cost on most API models while input compression raises it, and correct answers still diverge from reference text.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion
digest_headlines.headline: Single-axis evaluation is underdetermined, because cost, accuracy and reference agreement dissociate and a composite metric can mis-rank methods.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Candidates should be ranked at their deployment constraint level, since output-compression tolerance is not predicted by parameter count or unconstrained accuracy.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists pricing, dataset statistics, inference configuration, token and cost accounting, constraint specifications, and released artifacts.

repos.title: Depth Anything V2
repos.paper_summary: Depth Anything V2 is a monocular depth estimation model that produces fine-grained predictions by training on synthetic images and pseudo-labeled real data. The method replaces noisy real-image labels with precise synthetic ones to improve detail, then uses a large teacher model to generate pseudo-labels for 62M unlabeled real images, which are used to train smaller student models. This approach bridges the domain gap between synthetic and real scenes while preserving label quality. On their proposed DA-2K benchmark, the largest model (1.3B parameters) reaches 97.4% accuracy in relative depth discrimination, outperforming Stable Diffusion-based methods like Marigold (86.8%) by over 10 points. The smallest model (25M parameters) also exceeds all compared baselines. On standard benchmarks such as NYU-D and KITTI, performance is comparable to Depth Anything V1, but V2 shows stronger stability on transparent objects and complex layouts. Limitations include reliance on high-quality synthetic sources for initial training and potential residual errors from pseudo-label noise, though the paper notes that ignoring top-10% loss regions mitigates this.

repos.title: M3-Embedding: Multi-Linguality, Multi-Functionality, Multi-Granularity Text Embeddings Through Self-Knowledge Distillation
repos.paper_summary: M3-Embedding is a text embedding model that unifies dense, sparse, and multi-vector retrieval for over 100 languages and inputs up to 8,192 tokens. The model uses an XLM-RoBERTa encoder adapted via RetroMAE. It computes dense scores from the `[CLS]` token, sparse term weights via a learned linear projection, and multi-vector scores using late interaction. Training employs self-knowledge distillation: the weighted sum of relevance scores from all three methods serves as a teacher signal to refine each individual method’s InfoNCE loss. An efficient batching strategy groups data by sequence length and uses gradient checkpointing with cross-GPU broadcasting to increase batch size by more than 20 times for long sequences. On the MIRACL dev set (nDCG@10), M3-Embedding achieves an average of 71.5 across all methods combined, outperforming mE5-large (66.6) and E5-mistral-7b (63.4). On MKQA (Recall@100), it reaches an average of 75.5. Limitations include unverified generalizability to real-world scenarios outside tested benchmarks and undefined performance beyond the 8,192-token limit.
